model_info.name: Random Forest
data_sources: CPCB Annual Report on Solid Waste Management

reasons: PET collection rate in Mumbai is approximately 29% due to informal sector (kabadiwalas)
Sorting facilities reject about 14% of collected PET due to contamination
Mumbai has 3 operational PET recycling plants with limited daily capacity
tips: Rinse the bottle before discarding — reduces rejection at sorting facilities
Remove cap and label — they are different plastic types and contaminate PET batches
Flatten the bottle to save space — more can be collected per trip

reasons: HDPE has lower market value than PET, so informal collectors skip it more often
Only 22% of HDPE waste in Mumbai enters the recycling stream
HDPE containers with food residue are almost always rejected
tips: Clean the container thoroughly before recycling
Check for recycling symbol #2 — confirms it is HDPE
Sell to kabadiwala rather than putting in mixed recycling bin

reasons: PVC releases toxic chlorine when processed, most facilities refuse it
Only 5% of PVC in Mumbai is recycled, mostly by specialized facilities
PVC contaminates entire batches of other plastics if mixed in
tips: Avoid buying PVC products when alternatives exist
Contact BMC hazardous waste collection for large PVC items
Never burn PVC — it releases highly toxic dioxins

reasons: Plastic bags and films are too lightweight for economic collection
LDPE jams sorting machinery at recycling facilities
Only 8% of LDPE in Mumbai avoids landfill
tips: Reuse plastic bags multiple times before discarding
Switch to cloth bags — Mumbai has a plastic bag ban for bags under 50 microns
Collect clean LDPE bags and sell in bulk to kabadiwalas

reasons: PP has moderate recyclability but is often contaminated with food
About 18% of PP waste in Mumbai gets recycled
PP is commonly used in food containers making contamination rates high
tips: Wash food containers thoroughly before recycling
PP containers marked #5 have best recycling chances
Reuse PP containers for storage instead of discarding

reasons: Styrofoam is almost never recycled — less than 1% globally
It breaks into microplastics during processing and contaminates other materials
No recycling facility in Mumbai accepts polystyrene
tips: Avoid buying products with styrofoam packaging
Use alternatives like paper plates and cups
Styrofoam can only go to landfill — there is no recycling option in Mumbai

reasons: Mixed or unidentified plastics cannot be sorted into recyclable streams
Only 6% of mixed plastic in Mumbai avoids landfill
Recyclers need pure material streams — mixed plastics have no market
tips: Check the recycling number on the bottom to identify the plastic type
If no number exists, assume it is not recyclable
Reduce consumption of unidentified plastic products

reasons: Glass has a relatively strong recycling infrastructure in Mumbai at 42%
Kabadiwalas actively buy glass bottles — the economics work
Broken glass is harder to recycle and often rejected
tips: Keep glass bottles intact — broken glass has much lower recycling value
Rinse out food residue before recycling
Sell to kabadiwala — glass bottles have resale value in Mumbai

reasons: Aluminum has the highest recycling rate in Mumbai at 68%
High scrap value means ragpickers and kabadiwalas actively collect it
Aluminum can be recycled infinitely without quality loss
tips: Crush cans to save collection space
Rinse briefly — residue is less of an issue for aluminum
Sell to kabadiwala for best results — aluminum has good scrap value

reasons: Steel recycling rate in Mumbai is approximately 55%
Magnetic separation makes steel easy to sort at facilities
Food cans need labels removed and rinsing for best results
tips: Remove paper labels before recycling
Rinse out food residue
Kabadiwalas pay for steel/tin — sell directly for guaranteed recycling

reasons: Paper recycling rate in Mumbai is about 45% thanks to kabadiwala network
Wet or food-stained paper cannot be recycled and contaminates batches
Newspapers and office paper have highest recycling value
tips: Keep paper dry — wet paper cannot be recycled
Separate newspaper from mixed waste — it has the highest paper recycling value
Sell old newspapers and magazines to kabadiwala

reasons: Cardboard has a 52% recycling rate in Mumbai — one of the better materials
Amazon and Flipkart boxes are highly sought by kabadiwalas
Food-stained cardboard like pizza boxes often gets rejected
tips: Flatten boxes to save space and make collection easier
Remove tape and labels if possible
Keep dry — wet cardboard loses all recycling value

reasons: Tetra Pak is multi-layered (paper + plastic + aluminum) making separation expensive
Only 3% of Tetra Pak in Mumbai gets recycled
Only one facility in Maharashtra processes Tetra Pak
tips: Rinse the carton and flatten it
Look for Tetra Pak collection drives in your area
Consider switching to glass-bottled alternatives when available

reasons: Multi-layer packaging like chip packets combine plastic, aluminum, and paper
Separation is not economically viable — only 2% gets recycled globally
No facility in Mumbai can process multi-layer packaging at scale
tips: This item cannot be recycled in Mumbai currently
Reduce consumption of products with multi-layer packaging
Some organizations collect chip packets for upcycling into bags — search locally

reasons: Textile recycling in Mumbai is only about 12%
Most discarded clothing ends up in landfill
Blended fabrics (cotton+polyester) are harder to recycle than pure materials
tips: Donate wearable clothing instead of discarding
Use old clothes as cleaning rags
Drop at textile recycling bins — some Mumbai malls have them

reasons: Wood waste recycling in Mumbai is only 8%
Treated or painted wood cannot be recycled
Small wood items like chopsticks have no collection infrastructure
tips: Untreated wood can be composted
Repurpose wooden items before discarding
Painted or treated wood should go to regular waste, not recycling

reasons: Ceramic cannot be recycled — it does not melt or reform like glass
Broken ceramics contaminate glass recycling batches
Only 1% of ceramic waste is diverted from landfill
tips: Broken ceramics can only go to landfill waste
Repurpose broken pots as garden drainage material
Consider buying durable ceramics to reduce waste

reasons: Rubber recycling rate in Mumbai is about 5%
Vulcanized rubber cannot be easily reprocessed
Tire recycling exists but small rubber items have no collection system
tips: Old tires can be given to tire retreading shops
Small rubber items go to regular waste
Rubber takes 50-80 years to decompose in landfill

reasons: E-waste recycling in Mumbai is about 15% through formal channels
Informal e-waste recycling exists but often involves hazardous practices
E-waste contains toxic metals like lead and mercury requiring special handling
tips: Drop at authorized e-waste collection centers — BMC has designated points
Many electronics brands have take-back programs
Never throw e-waste in regular bins — toxic metals contaminate soil and water

reasons: Organic waste is not recycled but can be composted
Mumbai processes about 65% of segregated organic waste through composting
Mixed organic waste with non-organic items reduces composting success
tips: Segregate organic waste in the green bin
Home composting is easy for kitchen scraps
Keep organic waste separate from all other waste types
